claim_summary: Introduces GIFT-Eval-CTX, a 10,000-instance contextual-forecasting benchmark with structured Macro and Micro effects generated by validator-gated agents and paired history-only/context evaluation.

claim_evidence.quote: To this end, we introduce GIFT-EvalCTX, a contextual extension of the GIFT-Eval benchmark (Aksu et al., 2024).

To make the context portable across domains and less dependent on the language style of any particular LLM, we represent it as a compact key-value schema called structured effects, rather than as free-form text.
The final GIFT-Eval-CTX benchmark contains 10,000 instances from 20 GIFT-Eval source datasets and 78 dataset–frequency–term configurations.

evidence.quote: GIFT-Eval-CTX supports a paired evaluation of the same forecasting model under two information conditions.

process_validity.quote: If a proposal fails validation, the tool returns the numerical evidence so that the Agent can revise its proposal.

temporal_validity.quote: We construct GIFT-Eval-CTX from the held-out test regions of GIFT-Eval. Each multivariate series is flattened into univariate targets, and no window is cut from a training or validation region.

task_performance.quote: Structured effects substantially improve frontier LLM forecasts. Providing structured effects reduces overall MASE by 40.7% for GPT-5.6 Sol and 29.6% for Claude Opus 4.8, enabling both models to achieve performance comparable to or better than TSFMs.

notes: The current card's GTS/GH assignments use retired dimensions and treat annotation/critic logic as cross-task. Under the current R3 first-match test, both embed the task-specific effect-annotation output and validation criteria, so they are TSK; the paired protocol remains TSK.

items.reason: Effects are defined over the forecast horizon, Micro discovery is targeted at regions where TSFM reference forecasts have large residuals against the future ground truth, and validators are family-specific; the target, schema and validator criteria would be redesigned for another task family, so R3_1_TSK matches first.

The critic decides support/exclude/unresolved for Macro and Micro effect candidates, requires inspection of the complete interval, and re-triggers the effect validator; its criterion is the structured-effect annotation output, not a generic review order.

adjudication.summary: Both layer moves to TSK are accepted: the annotation pipeline and its critic embed the contextual-forecasting effect schema and residual-targeted validation criterion. The merged candidate was otherwise correct and is kept unchanged.
